newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel declines comment on French EMU chances.
newsitem.headline: Waigel declines comment on French EMU chances.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel declined to specifically comment on France's efforts to meet criteria for Europe's planned single currency.
Instead, he said simply that all candidate countries had to do their homework.

When asked about the possibility France may not meet the criteria for currency union, Waigel said "there are clear targets and clear agreements...Every country has the chance and the obligation to do their bit in 1997 to meet the criteria."

Waigel, speaking at a news conference during a visit to Berlin by leaders of his Christian Social Union party, said all countries, including France, had made clear that everyone must do their own work.
"We're doing that and so are others, and everyone must do their own work. I'm not evaluating the efforts of others," he said.
France's Socialist-led government has raised doubts about its ability to meet fiscal targets for monetary union.

Jacques Chirac, the conservative French president, in his first television address since the Socialist election victory in June, warned on Monday that France would be isolated and suffer tough consequences if it failed to qualify for monetary union.
